title: The Donkey and the Guru's Turban

keywords: the donkey and the guru's turban
full_text:
Guru Paramartha possessed a magnificent ceremonial turban made of fine crimson silk, embroidered with gold thread and adorned with a brass crescent, which he wore only when visiting rajahs and wealthy temple patrons.

One scorching afternoon, the Guru set out on his ancient gray donkey to attend a ceremonial feast in an adjoining village. Because the heat was oppressive, the Guru removed his heavy silk turban, handed it to Matti, and commanded with solemn authority: 'Matti, walk behind the donkey and watch this turban carefully! If anything falls from this beast along the road, pick it up immediately and place it securely in your shoulder bag! Do not lose a single item that drops from this journey!'

Matti bowed with earnest devotion: 'Master, my eyes shall be glued to the donkey's path! Whatever falls to the earth, I shall faithfully collect!'

The procession moved slowly along the dusty country road: the Guru dozing upon the donkey, and Matti marching behind, watching the ground with hawk-like vigilance.

A mile down the road, as the donkey plodded along, the beast lifted its tail and dropped a fresh, steaming heap of round, green manure cakes upon the dust.

Matti stopped, remembered his master's strict command: 'Whatever falls from the beast, pick it up immediately!'

Without hesitation, Matti gathered up the steaming cow-like donkey manure in his hands and stuffed it into his cotton shoulder bag, right alongside the Guru's fine crimson silk turban!

A mile further on, the donkey stumbled over a stone. The jolt caused the Guru's spare leather sandals, which were tied loosely to the saddle, to slip off and drop into the dust.

True to his orders, Matti picked up the dusty sandals and crammed them into the bag, pressing them down upon the manure and the silk turban.

When they reached the host's magnificent mansion, where noble guests and musicians were assembled, Guru Paramartha dismounted with aristocratic dignity. Turning to Matti, the Guru said: 'Fetch my ceremonial turban, Matti, so that I may enter the banquet hall adorned with dignity!'

Matti opened his shoulder bag and pulled out the crimson turban.

To the Guru's utter horror, the once-glorious silk turban was completely flattened, smeared with fresh, green donkey dung, coated with road dust, and smelling like a stable!

The assembled guests recoiled, holding their noses in disgust!

The Guru turned purple with rage: 'Matti! You wretched idiot! What have you done to my magnificent turban?'

Matti looked bewildered and hurt: 'Master, I merely obeyed your sacred command! You strictly ordered: "Whatever falls from this beast, pick it up immediately and put it in your bag!" The manure fell first, so I picked it up; the sandals fell second, so I picked them up; and I stored them all safely with your turban!'

Guru Paramartha was so mortified that he could not attend the banquet. Marching home with his bare, sweaty head, the Guru issued a revised decree: 'Henceforth, Matti, you shall not pick up everything that falls! I will provide you with a written list of approved items that may be collected!'

Madayan nodded in agreement: 'Yes, Master! Administrative protocol requires an itemized inventory of allowable drops!'
moral: Blind and literal obedience without common sense makes a servant the destroyer of what he was sent to guard.
